This appendix forms part of the article and has not been edited by the journal. It is referenced in the main text as "the appendix".

All results reported in this appendix are from the cohort-deduplicated (Set B) analysis, in which one publication per cohort contributes to each outcome.

## S1. Search strategy

| Field | Content |
|:-------------------------------|:---------------------------------------|
| Databases searched | PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE (Elsevier), SCOPUS |
| Search dates | Database inception to January 1999-April 2026 |
| Records retrieved | PubMed 1061; EMBASE 2603; SCOPUS 481 (total 4145) |
| Date limits applied | January 1999-April 2026 |
| Language limit | English |
| Publication types excluded via filter | None. Conference abstracts, editorials, letters, and case reports were excluded at screening rather than by search filter, to minimise inappropriate exclusion |
| Other sources searched | Reference list screening of included studies and prior systematic reviews; forward citation tracking (Web of Science) for key index publications; PROSPERO search for related and ongoing reviews |
| Deduplication and management | RIS export from each database, imported into Covidence for deduplication and screening |
| Search piloted against | Eight known included publications (Holtan 2022, Moiseev 2016, Tang 2023, Papanicolaou 2023, Salas 2023, Massoud 2021, Meyer 2024, Shaffer 2024) to verify recall |

: Search parameters.

The protocol specifies three concept blocks combined with AND, each block an OR of controlled vocabulary terms and free-text synonyms.

### PubMed/MEDLINE

```         
#1  Allogeneic HCT population
    ("Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation"[Mesh] OR "Bone Marrow Transplantation"[Mesh]
     OR "allogeneic stem cell transplant*"[tiab] OR "allo-HCT"[tiab] OR "allo-HSCT"[tiab]
     OR "haploidentical"[tiab] OR "HLA-matched"[tiab] OR "matched unrelated donor"[tiab]
     OR "mismatched unrelated donor"[tiab])

#2  PTCy intervention
    ("post-transplant cyclophosphamide"[tiab] OR "post-transplantation cyclophosphamide"[tiab]
     OR "posttransplant cyclophosphamide"[tiab] OR "posttransplantation cyclophosphamide"[tiab]
     OR "PTCy"[tiab] OR "PT-Cy"[tiab] OR "PTCY"[tiab]
     OR ("Cyclophosphamide"[Mesh] AND "Graft vs Host Disease"[Mesh]))

#3  Infection outcomes
    ("Infections"[Mesh] OR "Bacterial Infections"[Mesh] OR "Virus Diseases"[Mesh]
     OR "Mycoses"[Mesh] OR "Bacteremia"[Mesh] OR "Sepsis"[Mesh]
     OR "Cytomegalovirus Infections"[Mesh] OR "Invasive Fungal Infections"[Mesh]
     OR "bacterial infection*"[tiab] OR "viral infection*"[tiab] OR "fungal infection*"[tiab]
     OR "BSI"[tiab] OR "sepsis"[tiab] OR "CMV"[tiab] OR "EBV"[tiab] OR "HHV-6"[tiab]
     OR "BK virus"[tiab] OR "aspergillosis"[tiab] OR "candida"[tiab] OR "mucormycosis"[tiab]
     OR "mold"[tiab] OR "yeast"[tiab] OR "mortality"[tiab])

#4  #1 AND #2 AND #3
    Filters: Humans; English
```

### EMBASE (Emtree)

```         
#1  Allogeneic HCT population
    ('bone marrow transplantation'/exp OR 'stem cell transplantation'/exp
     OR 'allogeneic stem cell transplant*':ti,ab OR 'allo-hct':ti,ab OR 'allo-hsct':ti,ab
     OR haploidentical:ti,ab OR 'hla-matched':ti,ab OR 'matched unrelated donor':ti,ab
     OR 'mismatched unrelated donor':ti,ab)

#2  PTCy intervention
    ('post-transplant cyclophosphamide':ti,ab OR 'post-transplantation cyclophosphamide':ti,ab
     OR 'posttransplant cyclophosphamide':ti,ab OR 'posttransplantation cyclophosphamide':ti,ab
     OR ptcy:ti,ab OR 'pt-cy':ti,ab
     OR ('cyclophosphamide'/exp AND 'graft versus host reaction'/exp))

#3  Infection outcomes
    ('infection'/exp OR 'bacterial infection'/exp OR 'virus infection'/exp OR 'mycosis'/exp
     OR 'bacteremia'/exp OR 'sepsis'/exp OR 'cytomegalovirus infection'/exp
     OR 'invasive fungal infection'/exp
     OR 'bacterial infection*':ti,ab OR 'viral infection*':ti,ab OR 'fungal infection*':ti,ab
     OR bsi:ti,ab OR sepsis:ti,ab OR cmv:ti,ab OR ebv:ti,ab OR 'hhv-6':ti,ab
     OR 'bk virus':ti,ab OR aspergillosis:ti,ab OR candida:ti,ab OR mucormycosis:ti,ab
     OR mold:ti,ab OR yeast:ti,ab OR mortality:ti,ab)

#4  #1 AND #2 AND #3 AND [humans]/lim AND [english]/lim
```

### SCOPUS

```         
TITLE-ABS-KEY(
  ("allogeneic stem cell transplant*" OR "allo-HCT" OR "allo-HSCT"
   OR "hematopoietic stem cell transplantation" OR "bone marrow transplantation"
   OR haploidentical OR "HLA-matched" OR "matched unrelated donor"
   OR "mismatched unrelated donor")
  AND
  ("post-transplant cyclophosphamide" OR "post-transplantation cyclophosphamide"
   OR "posttransplant cyclophosphamide" OR "posttransplantation cyclophosphamide"
   OR PTCy OR "PT-Cy" OR (cyclophosphamide AND "graft versus host disease"))
  AND
  (infection* OR "bacterial infection*" OR "viral infection*" OR "fungal infection*"
   OR BSI OR sepsis OR bacteremia OR CMV OR "cytomegalovirus infection*" OR EBV
   OR "HHV-6" OR "BK virus" OR aspergillosis OR candida OR mucormycosis OR mold
   OR yeast OR "invasive fungal infection*" OR mortality)
) AND LANGUAGE(english)
```

## S6. Model specification and priors

Primary model (M1), for study $s$, arm $i$:

$$\text{events}_i \mid n_i \sim \text{Binomial}\!\left(n_i,\ \text{logit}^{-1}\!\left(\alpha + \big(\beta_{\text{PTCy}} + v_{s[i]}\big)\, x_i + \beta_{\text{tp}}\, t_i + u_{s[i]}\right)\right),
\qquad (u_s, v_s) \sim \mathcal{N}_2(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma})$$

where $x_i$ indicates a PTCy arm and $t_i$ indicates a late (≥1 year) rather than early (day +100 or +180) timepoint. Each study contributes a random intercept $u_s$ (baseline-risk variation) and a random PTCy-effect slope $v_s$, so the pooled coefficient $\beta_{\text{PTCy}}$ estimates the average study-level treatment effect and the between-study SD of $v_s$ (reported as τ) quantifies heterogeneity in the PTCy effect. With two arms per study the model is just-identified at study level, so for sparse outcomes (k ≤ 6) the prior on the SD parameters is correspondingly influential.

| Parameter                   | Prior                    |
|:----------------------------|:-------------------------|
| Fixed effects (β)           | N(0, 2·5)                |
| Intercept (α)               | N(0, 1·5)                |
| Between-study SDs (τ)       | Student t(3, 0, 1), half |
| Intercept–slope correlation | LKJ(1)                   |

: Prior specification for the primary model.

The steroid-mediation model (M2) adds arm-level systemic steroid exposure percentage, mean-centred, as an additional fixed effect, and is fitted on the complete-case subset of studies reporting steroid exposure.

MCMC: four chains × 4000 iterations (1000 warmup), `adapt_delta` = 0·95 (increased to 0·99 where divergent transitions occurred), giving 12 000 post-warmup draws per model.

## S9. Sensitivity analyses

![CMV sensitivity models, comparison 1: primary model, post-2020 restriction, and haploidentical-dominant restriction.](figures/FigureS9a_CMV_sensitivity){#fig-s9a}

![IFI leave-one-out analysis, comparison 1 (frequentist REML).](figures/FigureS9b_IFI_leave_one_out){#fig-s9b}

Full frequentist results for all models are provided in `freq_results_setB.csv`, a supplementary data file, which carries the deduplicated fits where deduplication applied and the original fits otherwise (see its `source` column). Under the random-slope specification, which — like the frequentist REML models — allows the treatment effect to vary across studies, Bayesian and frequentist estimates were concordant in direction for every outcome and closely matched in magnitude: the two outcomes that diverged most under the earlier common-effect (fixed treatment effect) specification, C1 BSI (Bayesian odds ratio 1·42 \[0·57–2·98\] versus frequentist 1·29 \[0·61–2·73\]) and C1 IFI (0·63 \[0·19–2·62\] versus 0·60 \[0·21–1·74\]), now agree. The pre-specified CMV sensitivity analyses estimated a larger effect in post-2020 studies (k = 17, 1·46 \[1·01–2·05\]) and an elevated but imprecise estimate in haploidentical-dominant cohorts (k = 12, 1·34 \[0·90–1·96\]).

### Indirect comparison of the C1 and C2 pooled effects

The depletion-depth interpretation in the main text contrasts the C1 and C2 pooled estimates. A formal indirect comparison — the posterior of the ratio of the two pooled odds ratios — is reported below. The two study sets are disjoint except for one three-arm study (Haebe 2023, study 167), whose shared contribution makes the test mildly conservative. The comparisons enrol different populations (predominantly haploidentical in C1, matched-donor in C2), so the contrast is confounded by population as well as comparator.

| Outcome | C1 OR (95% CrI) | C2 OR (95% CrI) | Ratio (95% CrI) | P(C1 \> C2) |
|:--------------|:--------------|:--------------|:--------------|--------------:|
| CMV reactivation | 1·22 (0·90–1·65) | 0·86 (0·50–1·42) | 1·43 (0·80–2·63) | 0·89 |
| BK virus reactivation | 2·39 (1·48–3·66) | 2·49 (1·09–6·03) | 0·95 (0·36–2·44) | 0·46 |

: Posterior indirect contrast of the pooled PTCy effects between comparisons. P(C1 \> C2) is the posterior probability that the C1 pooled effect exceeds the C2 pooled effect.

The CMV contrast is not resolved: the depletion-depth hierarchy is compatible with the data but not demonstrated by it. The BK contrast is compatible with no difference between comparators, consistent with a comparator-invariant — cyclophosphamide-specific — elevation.

## S10. Publication bias

Funnel-plot asymmetry was assessed on the cohort-deduplicated datasets (Egger's regression, Peters' sample-size test, Begg's rank test, and Duval–Tweedie trim-and-fill; full results in `pub_bias_results.csv`, supplementary data file). C1 overall survival showed asymmetry by Egger (p = 0·016) and Begg (p = 0·047) but not by the sample-size-based Peters test (p = 0·23); trim-and-fill imputed seven studies, shifting the frequentist estimate from 0·79 to 0·91 \[0·74–1·11\]. C1 acute GVHD showed asymmetry across tests (Egger p = 0·023; Begg p = 0·018; Peters p = 0·095), with trim-and-fill shifting the estimate from 0·61 to 0·83 \[0·61–1·13\]. No other outcome showed significant asymmetry (all p \> 0·09).

Robust Bayesian model-averaging (RoBMA v4.0.0; ensemble of selection-function, PET, and PEESE publication-bias models) was fitted to every outcome with k ≥ 6 on the cohort-deduplicated datasets. Model-averaged estimates and inclusion Bayes factors for the presence of an effect (BF~eff~) and of publication bias (BF~bias~) are shown below. All ensembles converged (R̂ ≤ 1·01; ESS \> 1000).

| Outcome | Comparison | k | Model-averaged OR (95% CrI) | BF~eff~ | BF~bias~ |
|:--------|:-----------|--:|:----------------------------|--------:|---------:|
| Overall survival | C1 | 35 | 1·00 (0·81–1·19) | 0·20 | 18·6 |
| Non-relapse mortality | C1 | 12 | 1·00 (0·81–1·29) | 0·21 | 0·73 |
| Relapse-related mortality | C1 | 34 | 0·95 (0·79–1·00) | 0·60 | 0·85 |
| Acute GVHD II–IV | C1 | 28 | 0·97 (0·58–1·33) | 0·35 | 14·0 |
| Chronic GVHD mod–severe | C1 | 19 | 0·55 (0·33–1·00) | 6·7 | 2·2 |
| Chronic GVHD any | C1 | 8 | 0·45 (0·19–1·03) | 4·3 | 5·9 |
| CMV reactivation | C1 | 22 | 1·05 (0·97–1·49) | 0·39 | 0·47 |
| Bloodstream infection | C1 | 6 | 1·11 (0·76–2·16) | 0·59 | 0·87 |
| Invasive fungal infection | C1 | 6 | 0·80 (0·34–1·30) | 0·90 | 0·63 |
| BK virus reactivation | C1 | 11 | 2·00 (1·00–3·15) | 12·0 | 0·85 |
| Infection-related mortality | C1 | 13 | 1·00 (0·84–1·23) | 0·20 | 0·42 |
| Overall survival | C2 | 9 | 0·96 (0·61–1·23) | 0·34 | 1·7 |
| Acute GVHD II–IV | C2 | 8 | 0·87 (0·39–1·62) | 0·78 | 2·8 |
| Chronic GVHD mod–severe | C2 | 6 | 0·98 (0·62–1·45) | 0·32 | 0·99 |
| CMV reactivation | C2 | 12 | 0·99 (0·71–1·33) | 0·28 | 1·1 |
| Relapse-related mortality | C2 | 10 | 0·92 (0·67–1·10) | 0·74 | 1·9 |
| Infection-related mortality | C2 | 7 | 0·98 (0·77–1·06) | 0·24 | 0·52 |

: RoBMA model-averaged estimates on the cohort-deduplicated datasets. BF~eff~ and BF~bias~ are inclusion Bayes factors for the presence of an effect and of publication bias, respectively; values \> 3 are conventionally taken as moderate, \> 10 as strong evidence. {#tbl-s10-robma}

Three findings stand out. First, publication bias is supported only for the two headline C1 benefit outcomes — overall survival (BF~bias~ 18·6) and acute GVHD (BF~bias~ 14·0) — and for both, the bias-adjusted model-averaged estimate is essentially null (OS 1·00 \[0·81–1·19\]; aGVHD 0·97 \[0·58–1·33\]), consistent with the trim-and-fill results above. Second, BK virus reactivation is the only outcome with strong evidence of a non-null effect after model-averaging (BF~eff~ 12·0; adjusted estimate 2·00 \[1·00–3·15\]), with no evidence of bias; moderate effect evidence supports chronic GVHD (BF~eff~ 6·7 moderate–severe, 4·3 any), with weak-to-moderate bias evidence for the any-definition subset (BF~bias~ 5·9). Third, no other outcome yielded more than weak evidence for either an effect or publication bias. The RoBMA results should temper confidence in the unadjusted C1 survival and acute GVHD estimates reported in table 2.

## S11. GRADE certainty-of-evidence profiles

Certainty was assessed per the GRADE Handbook, adapted for observational evidence (starting certainty LOW). The profiles below were reassessed (2026-09-30) against the cohort-deduplicated, random-slope estimates of table 2 and the Set B publication-bias analyses of S10, and supersede all earlier profiles. Risk-of-bias and indirectness judgements are unchanged from the original assessment; the only risk-of-bias downgrade applied is to C1 NRM (steroid-mediation confounding).

| Outcome | Comparison | k | OR (95% CrI) | Inconsistency | Imprecision | Publication bias | Certainty |
|:--------|:--------|--------:|:--------|:--------|:--------|:--------|:--------|
| Overall survival | C1 | 35 | 0·76 (0·62–0·93) | −1 (τ = 0·44) | 0 | −1 (RoBMA BF~bias~ = 18·6; bias-adjusted OR 1·00 \[0·81–1·19\]) | ⊕⊖⊖⊖ VERY LOW |
| Overall survival | C2 | 9 | 0·75 (0·42–1·31) | −1 (τ = 0·68) | −1 (CrI crosses null) | not assessable | ⊕⊖⊖⊖ VERY LOW |
| Non-relapse mortality | C1 | 12 | 0·81 (0·46–1·22) | 0 | −1 (CrI crosses null) | 0 | ⊕⊖⊖⊖ VERY LOW |
| Acute GVHD II–IV | C1 | 28 | 0·58 (0·44–0·77) | −1 (τ = 0·54) | 0 | −1 (Egger p = 0·023; trim-and-fill 0·83 crosses null) | ⊕⊖⊖⊖ VERY LOW |
| Acute GVHD II–IV | C2 | 8 | 0·51 (0·24–1·02) | −1 (τ = 0·81) | −1 (CrI reaches null) | not assessable | ⊕⊖⊖⊖ VERY LOW |
| CMV reactivation | C1 | 22 | 1·22 (0·90–1·65) | −1 (τ = 0·53) | −1 (CrI crosses null) | 0 | ⊕⊖⊖⊖ VERY LOW |
| CMV reactivation | C2 | 12 | 0·86 (0·50–1·42) | −1 (τ = 0·68) | −1 (CrI crosses null) | 0 | ⊕⊖⊖⊖ VERY LOW |
| Bloodstream infection | C1 | 6 | 1·42 (0·57–2·98) | −1 (τ = 0·71; heterogeneous definitions) | −1 (CrI crosses null) | not assessable (k = 6) | ⊕⊖⊖⊖ VERY LOW |
| Invasive fungal infection | C1 | 6 | 0·63 (0·19–2·62) | −1 (τ = 1·28; extreme) | −1 (CrI crosses null) | not assessable (k = 6) | ⊕⊖⊖⊖ VERY LOW |

: GRADE domain profiles for the pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes, reassessed against the cohort-deduplicated random-effects estimates (2026-09-30). Starting certainty LOW (observational evidence). C2 BSI and C2 IFI were not modelled (insufficient studies) and are not rated.

## S13. PROSPERO registration

The study protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261372156) before data extraction. Protocol amendments were: (1) a Bayesian rather than frequentist primary analysis framework; (2) addition of BK virus reactivation, infection-related mortality, and relapse-related mortality as secondary outcomes; and (3) addition of the steroid-mediation (M2) model.
